items.Sentence: Fine screens will be provided upstream of the MBR tanks to remove particulate material...A horizontal-packaged drum screen system with a sluiceway for screening disposal will be used to control odors.

The MBR process will consist of biological treatment utilizing anoxic, aerobic, and deoxygenation tanks, followed by submerged membrane ultrafiltration...remove carbonaceous biochemical oxygen demand, nitrogen through nitrification and denitrification, and microbial solids removal through membrane separation.

pretreatment (chloramine injection, sulfuric acid and antiscalant addition)...Chloramine will be injected after the RO feed tank to prevent biological fouling...Sulfuric acid and antiscalant will be injected after the RO feed tank to control mineral scaling.
Cartridge filters will be provided upstream of the RO membranes to remove particulate matter.

The HAWPF treatment process will consist of fine screens, membrane bioreactors (MBR), reverse osmosis (RO)...RO removes large molecular weight dissolved organic and inorganic compounds and pathogens by forcing MBR effluent through a semipermeable membrane.

Chloramine will be dosed upstream of the UV reactors (two on duty and one standby) to generate hydroxyl radicals...and to provide a chlorine residual to achieve additional disinfection in the effluent pipeline.
Post-treatment stabilization includes calcite contactors...used to adjust pH, add alkalinity and hardness...Calcite and sodium hydroxide will be used for adjustment of pH, alkalinity, and hardness.
Sodium hypochlorite and liquid ammonium sulfate will be added post-stabilization to provide a 2 mg/L chloramine residual in the product water tank and the distribution piping.

a single odor control unit consisting of a single-bed carbon adsorber, which will remove hydrogen sulfide and a variety of organic sulfides that are commonly emitted from primary effluent screens and the biological nutrient removal and MBR processes.
HAWPF recycled water will be pumped to the product water tank for storage and equalization.
